{{Quote|Yup, that's it. Dagobah. [&hellip;] No, I'm not gonna change my mind about this. I'm not picking up any cities or technology. Massive life-form readings, though. There's something alive down there.|Luke Skywalker|<ref name="SWEV">{{Film|V}}</ref>}}
'''Dagobah''' (/'deɪgəbə/; {{Audio|Dagobah.flac|pronunciation}}) was an [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Dagobah system/Legends|Dagobah system]]. A remote world of [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]] and [[Tree/Legends|forests]], it served as a refuge for [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] during his [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]] after the events of [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] had taken place.

==Geography==
{{Quote|Yes, I'm sure it's perfectly safe for droids.|[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] to [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]]|<ref name="SWEV" />}}
Dagobah was located in the [[Sluis sector/Legends|Sluis sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. Despite the fact that it was located near the [[Rimma Trade Route/Legends|Rimma Trade Route]], it was reachable only by obscure [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]].<ref name="atlas" />

[[File:Dragonsnake_Bog.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The [[Dragonsnake Bog/Legends|swamp-covered]] surface of Dagobah]]
Dagobah was a harsh, humid, swampy [[Planet/Legends|planet]], mostly covered in shallow marshland, interspersed with stifling forests and at least one [[Cave of Evil/Legends|cave]]. There were very few truly open bodies of water on the planet: the water supply was thinly invested throughout the planet's main habitat, swampland, although there were vast expanses of mud fields. Dagobah was home to many creatures, such as [[Bogwing/Legends|bogwings]], [[Dragonsnake/Legends|dragonsnakes]],<ref name="TD" /> [[Nudj/Legends|nudj]], [[Sleen/Legends|sleens]], [[Vine snake/Legends|vine snakes]], and [[Swamp slug/Legends|swamp slugs]]. Examples of flora included the [[Adder moss/Legends|Adder moss]], the [[hassling]],<ref name="Star Wars Episode I: The Gungan Frontier">[[Star Wars Episode I: The Gungan Frontier|''Star Wars'' Episode I: ''The Gungan Frontier'']]</ref> [[Gnarltree/Legends|Gnarltree]]<ref name="Darksaber" /> and [[Meat flower]]. The planet was devoid of any technology advanced civilization, although the reclusive, pre-industrial [[Hepsalum Tash]] did call it home.<ref name="daa" />

==History==
===Surveys===
{{Quote|Mudhole?! Slimy?! My home this is!|[[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]|audio=SlimyMudhole.flac|<ref name="SWEV" />}}
In [[700 BBY]], the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Minch (Jedi)|Minch]] [[Duel on Dagobah (700 BBY)|battled]] and killed a powerful [[Bpfasshi/Legends|Bpfasshi]] [[Bpfasshi Dark Jedi leader|Dark Jedi]] on the planet. The Dark Jedi's energies absorbed into its surroundings, tainting the cave where he was slain with the dark side.<ref name="HOD">{{Tales|16|Heart of Darkness}}</ref>

The planet seldom appeared in astrography charts and it was discovered and re-scouted several times. The first official Republic survey of Dagobah occurred in [[39 BBY/Legends|39 BBY]].<ref name="TISWU">''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> A team of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaanian]] explorers were stranded there but were devoured by wildlife, while a pre-[[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] expedition was forced to resort to cannibalism.<ref name="atlas" />

===Clone Wars===
In early [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], a Republic research team under [[Halka Four-Den/Legends|Halka Four-Den]] was stationed on Dagobah to research the native flora and fauna. From even the initial assessment, the team concluded that Dagobah was crawling with an incredible diversity of life, and made notes to recommend Dagobah for more extensive surveys, given the likely advances in genetics and medicine that even a few of its lifeforms would cause. Unfortunately, Halka Four-Den and her research team died on Dagobah before they could be retrieved.<ref name="TISWU" /> Likely due to the outbreak of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], their distress signals were ignored until it was too late. The few survivors were forced to raise [[The Children|their children]] as cannibals.<ref name="GOF:TH" />
At the outbreak of the war, [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] discovered thirty-eight worlds deleted from the [[Jedi Archives/Legends|Jedi Archives]], Dagobah was one of them.<ref name="db" />

During the war, Dagobah was located within [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]]-controlled space.<ref name="atlas" />

In a late stage of the war, and under the guidance of the spirit of Qui-Gon Jinn, Yoda briefly traveled to Dagobah seeking answers to explain mysterious "voices" only he could hear. There, he was given the spiritual task of finding out how to become one with the Force and achieve true immortality. Yoda noted how strong the planet was with the Force, and learned from Qui-Gon's Force-spirit that it was one of the purest places in the Galaxy. During this short visit, Yoda entered the tainted cave and experienced a powerful vision showing him the extent of the Sith's tightening hold on the galaxy, the impending destruction of the Jedi Order, and the confirmed existence of Darth Sidious.<ref name="Voices" />

===Yoda's exile===
<div style="float:right">[[File:YodaLandsonDagobah.jpg|thumb|250px|Yoda begins his exile on Dagobah.]]</div>
{{Quote|Into exile, I must go. Failed, I have.|Yoda|<ref name="SWEIII">{{Film|III}}</ref>}}
In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="date-blog">{{Blog|holocron|13/comments|Major Character Birth Years}}</ref> at the [[Order 66/Legends|beginning]] of the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] went into exile<ref name="SWEIII" /> in the swamps of Dagobah via an [[E3-standard starship lifeboat/Legends|escape pod]] from [[Polis Massa/Legends|Polis Massa]],<ref name="db2">{{DB|starship|yodaescapepod|escape pod, Yoda's}}</ref> after [[Skirmish in the Senate|facing]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]].<ref name="SWEIII" /> By choosing a world that "didn't exist"<ref name="db" /> and the [[Cave of Evil/Legends|Cave of Evil]] negating his [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]] presence, Yoda remained hidden.<ref name="htte">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref>

At some point, Yoda encountered the [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] of [[Galen Marek]], who like Marek took on the name [[Subject 1138|Starkiller]], when the clone went to Dagobah to find himself. He allowed Starkiller inside the Dark Cave, telling him that he was simply a watcher.<ref name="SWTFUII">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''</ref>

[[Tash Arranda/Legends|Tash Arranda]] and [[Zak Arranda/Legends|Zak Arranda]] met Yoda on the planet, but he chose not to train them in the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] ways at that time, explaining to them he was awaiting a different student. Afterwards, the Arrandas assisted in the rescue of the [[The Children|descendants of the survey team]] dispatched in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], thus ridding Dagobah of the closest thing to an "advanced civilization" it had probably ever boasted. They were likely rehabilitated by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]].<ref name="GOF:TH" />

Despite it being a remote planet, it as well as the system it belonged to nonetheless was included as a destination in the ''[[Intergalactic Passport]]'', with it being specifically recommended that any space travelers who stop at Dagobah must carry all-purpose antihistamine tablets and topical ointments at all times during visits there in order to lessen the effects of various insect bites that likely occur there.<ref name="Star Wars Intergalactic Passport">''[[The Star Wars Intergalactic Passport]]''</ref>

====The next Skywalker====
{{Quote|You will go to the Dagobah system. There you will learn from Yoda, the Jedi Master who instructed me.|[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] to Luke Skywalker|<ref name="SWEV" />}}
[[File:Dagobah_Training_Grounds-TCG_Core_Set.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Yoda training [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] on Dagobah]]
In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="date-blog" /> during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] was visited on the ice planet [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] by the [[Force ghost/Legends|ghost]] of [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], who instructed him to seek Yoda on Dagobah in order that he might be trained in the ways of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]. Skywalker traveled to Dagobah in his [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing]], along with [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], after the end of the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]. Due to a bumpy landing, Luke's X-wing ended up being half-buried in the swamp, and a grumpy and irritable Luke met a strange creature that turned out to be Yoda. During his grueling training, Luke learned control and power in the Force.<ref name="SWEV" />

While on Dagobah, Luke confronted a [[Droid/Legends|Droid]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|Bounty hunter]] named [[Milko]], whose mission was to kill Luke. Luke defeated the droid in armed battle. Luke had a feeling that the [[Duel on Dagobah (3 ABY)/Legends|encounter]] was a test arranged by Yoda but had no idea whether he had passed or failed.<ref name="Slippery Slope">{{Tales|15|Slippery Slope}}</ref> [[File:Dabogah.jpg|thumb|250px|Dagobah from orbit]]Luke later entered the cave where the Dark Jedi had been defeated to test himself and experienced a vision where he fought a version of Darth Vader with Luke's face underneath his mask, hinting at both Vader's identity as his father and his own later involvement with the dark side. Later in his training, Skywalker had a vision of his friends [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], and [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]] suffering on [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]]. As a result, he left his training early, promising Yoda that he would return to complete it.<ref name="SWEV" />

He did return in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], but only in time to have one final conversation with Yoda before his teacher's death. Afterward, he spoke extensively with [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] about the conflicting stories of Luke's parentage.<ref name="SWEVI">{{Film|VI}}</ref>

===Jedi involvement===
The [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] established a base on [[Mount Yoda]] in [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]].<ref name="Mission" />

[[File:Dagobah_TEA.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Dagobah]]
Luke Skywalker would return to Dagobah in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]], this time seeing a vision of the past in the cave and finding the Dark Jedi's [[Beckon call/Legends|beckon call]].<ref name="htte" /> He would return again in [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]] with his then-love [[Callista Ming]], trying to re-establish her connection to the Force.<ref name="Darksaber" /> In [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]], the dark side power of the [[Cave of Evil/Legends|cave]] there was siphoned by the [[Disciples of Ragnos]]. This supposedly removed all of the dark energy, but it presumably returned to its source when the Scepter of Ragnos was destroyed or otherwise somehow regenerated itself.<ref name="SWJKJA">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref>

In [[22 ABY/Legends|22 ABY]], [[Anakin Solo]] along with [[Ikrit]], [[Tahiri Veila]], [[Uldir Lochett]], [[Peckhum]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] returned to Dagobah because Anakin had been troubled by visions of himself as a [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]]; this was due to his heritage as the grandson of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], who had become the infamous [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]]. After surviving encounters with the planet's dangerous fauna, Anakin and his companions finally reached the [[Cave of Evil/Legends|same cave to which Luke had gone]] years before. There, Anakin faced the manifestations of his own doubts, but emerged victorious.<ref name="JJK: AQ">''[[Junior Jedi Knights: Anakin's Quest]]''</ref>

Towards the end of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], Tahiri Veila traveled to Dagobah to undertake a similar test to Anakin Solo's, but instead fell in love with a [[Yuuzhan Vong]] [[Shamed Ones|Shamed One]], who believed the planet was sacred to the Jedi. Vowing to carry his message back to [[Nom Anor|Yu'shaa]], she left Dagobah for [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]], not venturing into the cave.

In [[36 ABY]], [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] sent Jedi Knights Tahiri, [[Lowbacca]] and [[Tesar Sebatyne]] to Dagobah to meditate in exile. They had been deemed a threat to Jedi security due to the three [[Joiner]]s passing Jedi information to [[Aryn Dro Thul]] during the [[Swarm War]]. Luke told them that he would call them once he felt they were ready to rejoin the order, and that they were not to leave until they felt that call.<ref name="DNIII">''[[Dark Nest III: The Swarm War]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:MCQ-dagobah.jpg|thumb|250px|Concept art by [[Ralph McQuarrie]]]]
Dagobah first appeared in the [[1980]] film [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], the second installment of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[original trilogy]].<ref name="SWEV" /> The [[1991]] novel ''[[Heir to the Empire]]'',<ref name="htte" /> and its accompanying [[1992]] reference book ''[[Heir to the Empire Sourcebook]]'',<ref name="httes">''[[Heir to the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> placed Dagobah and its [[Dagobah system/Legends|eponymous system]] in the [[Sluis sector/Legends|Sluis sector]].<ref name="htte" /><ref name="httes" />

Slated to appear in one scene in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']], the planet was cut from the final film, leaving it for the DVD release.

''Heir to the Empire'' describes how Yoda went to Dagobah in pursuit of a Dark Jedi from [[Bpfassh]] and killed him on the planet. In [[Star Wars Insider 98|''Star Wars Insider'' 98]], [[Leland Chee]] wrote that this is no longer considered part of continuity because Yoda had never been on Dagobah before his exile. It has been suggested the battle occurred shortly after the exile; however, such a theory was never confirmed. The concept of Yoda having never been on Dagobah prior to his exile was, in turn, later countermanded directly by "[[Voices]]," an installment of the CGI animated series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'', which revealed that Yoda had, in fact, been to Dagobah, having been summoned there by the spirit of [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] to learn about the [[Force ghost/Legends|path to immortality]], and as such this Insider article no longer is correct.

[[File:Dagobah_X-wing_Topps_Photocard.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Early promotional photo of Dagobah and Luke's X-wing]]
A planet map displayed at the original [[Star Tours (real-world)|Star Tours]] attraction in [[Disneyland Paris]] and [[Tokyo Disneyland]] erroneously places the planet within the [[Tion Hegemony/Legends|Tion Hegemony]].

A segment of [[Wizards.com]]'s [[Planet Hoppers]] feature was planned for Dagobah, but it was never released.<ref name="Bespin PH">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20041028bespin5|series=Bespin: Action Tidings|text=Part 5: An Exclusive!}}</ref>

The Dagobah set was built at Elstree Studios. Because of the demand for such a huge set, a new soundstage was built. "Stage 6" which later was renamed "The George Lucas Stage". For the interior scenes, real dirt and water was shipped into the studio, and after days of shooting was miserably foul smelling and humid. The stage was 3 feet above ground to accommodate the puppetry scenes for Yoda.
